workout.title: Andrew Ankle Rehab
workout.notes: Each daily occurrence is a separate session with independent completion and logging.

activities.title: Ankle Alphabet
activities.prescription: A–Z once or twice per session
steps: Sit comfortably in a chair, or lie down with your leg supported. Keep your knee relatively still.
Lift your foot slightly off the floor. Use your foot as a “pen” to slowly trace A through Z in the air.
Make the letters as large as comfortable, moving only your ankle and foot. Move slowly and deliberately.
If you experience pain, make the letters smaller or stay within a comfortable range of motion.
Perform A–Z once or twice each session. Repeat on the opposite side if instructed.

images.alt: Original exercise directions for ankle alphabet

activities.purpose: Improve ankle mobility, reduce stiffness, and promote circulation.
activities.notes: Focus on smooth, controlled movement in all directions: up, down, in, and out. The sheet says 1–3 times per day; the overall workout is scheduled twice daily.

activities.title: Ankle Inversion with CLX
steps: While seated, place one CLX loop on your foot, then cross your legs as shown in the illustration.
With your other leg, step on the CLX band and hold the other end.
Move your foot up and down as shown. Repeat for the specified number of reps.

images.alt: Exercise sheet illustration: Ankle Inversion with CLX

activities.title: Resisted Ankle Eversion with Elastic Band
steps: While seated, attach an elastic band to your foot as pictured.
Draw your foot outward to the side. Keep your heel in contact with the floor the entire time.
Hold for 5 seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat for the specified number of reps.

images.alt: Exercise sheet illustration: Resisted Ankle Eversion with Elastic Band

activities.title: Resisted Ankle Plantarflexion with Elastic Band — Seated
steps: In a seated position, place an elastic band around your foot as shown.
Draw back on the elastic band so your foot raises toward the ceiling, keeping your heel on the ground.
Press your foot downward and forward, exaggerating the lead with your big toe.
Repeat for the specified number of reps.

images.alt: Exercise sheet illustration: Resisted Ankle Plantarflexion with Elastic Band — Seated

activities.title: Resisted Ankle Dorsiflexion with Elastic Band
steps: Start seated with your unaffected leg bent and an elastic band attached to your affected foot.
Draw your foot upward as pictured and hold for 5 seconds.
Return to the starting position. Keep your heel in contact with the floor the entire time.

images.alt: Exercise sheet illustration: Resisted Ankle Dorsiflexion with Elastic Band

activities.title: Single-Leg Stance
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart. If needed, rest or hover your hands on a chair or sturdy object in front of you.
Slowly bend your knee to 90 degrees as shown, balancing on the other leg.
Hold your knee bent for 15 seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.

activities.title: Standing Calf Stretch (Gastroc)
steps: Stand in front of a wall or chair and place your hands on it. Lean slightly forward.
Step forward with your non-involved leg. Keep toes and feet pointing forward with a slight bend in your front knee.
Extend your involved leg back. Do not bend your back knee.
Lean slightly forward and hold for 30 seconds. You should feel a stretch in your back leg.
Repeat for 3 reps.

images.alt: Exercise sheet illustration: Standing Calf Stretch (Gastroc)
